metadata.title: Side-Specific Soft Constraints in Quadratic Programming
metadata.description:
Soft constraints price departures from selected operating preferences while preserving physical hard limits. We implement side-specific separable linear-quadratic interval costs in a native OSQP-style projection path and compare equivalent formulations through independent lifting, generalized slack projection, DAQP, a fixed-parameter FlexQP reconstruction and ElastiQP. Fifteen cases cover scalar semantics, grouped penalties, semidefinite curvature, control conflict and a building-energy model. An initial preregistered computation comprises 456 seeded instances, retaining 11592 accepted and 7560 incompatible measured observations. Its median paired relative cold end-to-end reduction is 0.50%, with a 95% seed-cluster interval of [-3.29%,3.94%], so the predicted 10% improvement is not established. A separate native directional group-peak implementation retains original interval rows and is evaluated against exact row-split and compact-epigraph alternatives in 210 synthetic repeated-forecast instances. In its 144-instance heldout population, the median paired reduction score is -212.449875%, with 95% limits -225.336618% and -192.873759%, retaining 9 failed pairs. That prediction is also not established. Original-space checks, immutable numerical evidence and explicit failure states distinguish mathematical agreement from computational advantage. The static workbench, native package, local execution and offline research lanes have separate capabilities. Neither smaller principal dimensions nor a published engineering package establishes algorithmic novelty, operational safety or a general runtime advantage.

Code, editable LaTeX sources and reproducible evidence: CAOS_SoftQP. Native implementation: CAOS_SoftQP_Engine. Coupled-study evidence: archived dataset.
